18.7.s: atha sūda dohāḥ |
18.7.d: अथ सूद दोहाः ।

18.8.s: yā indra bhuja ābhara ity etayā bārhatīm aśītim pratipadyate |
18.8.d: या इन्द्र भुज आभर इत्य् एतया बार्हतीम् अशीतिम् प्रतिपद्यते ।
18.8.m: With [the verse beginning] 'What enjoyments, O Indra, bring [them]' he begins the Bārhata eighty.
Those are nine genuine Bṛhatī verses.

18.8.s: viśve ta indra vīryam iti tisraḥ |
18.8.d: विश्वे त इन्द्र वीर्यम् इति तिस्रः ।
18.8.m: [The hymn beginning] 'All your heroic power, O Indra' consists of three.

18.8.s: tam ghem itthā namasvina iti dve |
18.8.d: तम् घेम् इत्था नमस्विन इति द्वे ।
18.8.m: [The hymn beginning] 'Indeed, him thus with reverence' consists of two.

18.8.s: na sīma deva āpad iti ṣaṭ |
18.8.d: न सीम देव आपद् इति षट् ।
18.8.m: [The hymn beginning] 'Him neither god reached' consists of six.
Those are twenty genuine Bṛhatī verses.
[The hymn beginning] 'He who continually [helps], active among men' consists of four.

18.8.s: mo ṣu tvā vāghataś cana iti catvāra uddhṛtya dvipadām |
18.8.d: मो षु त्वा वाघतश् चन इति चत्वार उद्धृत्य द्विपदाम् ।
18.8.m: [The hymn beginning] 'Let not the sacrificers [detain] you' consists of four, setting aside the Dvipadā verse.

18.8.s: ud in v asya ricyata iti pañca |
18.8.d: उद् इन् व् अस्य रिच्यत इति पञ्च ।
18.8.m: [The hymn beginning] 'Now his [wealth] indeed overflows' consists of five.

18.8.s: tat tvā yāmi suvīryam yukṣvā hi vṛtrahantama iti dvau dvau |
18.8.d: तत् त्वा यामि सुवीर्यम् युक्ष्वा हि वृत्रहन्तम इति द्वौ द्वौ ।
18.8.m: [The hymns beginning] 'That heroic might of yours I ask' and 'Harness indeed, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra' consist of two each.

18.8.s: yad indra prāg apāg udag iti sapta |
18.8.d: यद् इन्द्र प्राग् अपाग् उदग् इति सप्त ।
18.8.m: [The hymn beginning] 'Whether, O Indra, eastward, westward, northward' consists of seven.
[The hymn beginning] 'Rain down, O you of abundant wealth' consists of two.

18.8.s: avipro vā yad avidhad iti pañca |
18.8.d: अविप्रो वा यद् अविधद् इति पञ्च ।
18.8.m: [The hymn beginning] 'Or whether the non-sage worshipped' consists of five.

18.8.s: yaḥ śakro mṛkṣo aśvya iti ṣaṭ |
18.8.d: यः शक्रो मृक्षो अश्व्य इति षट् ।
18.8.m: [The hymn beginning] 'He who is mighty, cleansing, related to horses' consists of six.

18.9.m: Then he recites genuine Bṛhatī verses.

18.9.s: mahe cana tvām adriva iti pañcaviṃśatiḥ |
18.9.d: महे चन त्वाम् अद्रिव इति पञ्चविंशतिः ।
18.9.m: [The hymn beginning] 'Not even for great [gain], O wielder of the stone' consists of twenty-five.

18.9.s: tāsām viṃśatim śastvā atha sūda dohasam |
18.9.d: तासाम् विंशतिम् शस्त्वा अथ सूद दोहसम् ।
18.9.m: Having recited twenty of them, then [he recites] the Sūdadohas verse.
[The verse beginning] 'Desiring cows' is the verse containing the nivid.

18.9.s: tām pacchaḥ śastvā āhūya nividam dadhāti |
18.9.d: ताम् पच्छः शस्त्वा आहूय निविदम् दधाति ।
18.9.m: Having recited it quarter by quarter, having called out, he inserts the nivid.

18.9.s: tām paccho vyavagrāham śastvā sama sūktām |
18.9.d: ताम् पच्छो व्यवग्राहम् शस्त्वा सम सूक्ताम् ।
18.9.m: Having recited it quarter by quarter, pausing after each, [he recites] the one that completes the hymn;

18.9.s: uttamena padena praṇutya sa jātebhir iti nividā śaṃsati |
18.9.d: उत्तमेन पदेन प्रणुत्य स जातेभिर् इति निविदा शंसति ।
18.9.m: having recited [it] with the last quarter [intoned without pause], he recites along with the nivid [beginning] 'With those born [together]'.

18.9.s: tām pacchaḥ śastvāa tha sūda dohasam |
18.9.d: ताम् पच्छः शस्त्वाअ थ सूद दोहसम् ।
18.9.m: Having recited it quarter by quarter, then [he recites] the Sūdadohas verse.

18.10.m: Then he recites genuine Bṛhatī verses.
He begins with those that were left over from the twenty-five.

18.10.s: vayam gha tvā sutāvanta iti pañcadaśa |
18.10.d: वयम् घ त्वा सुतावन्त इति पञ्चदश ।
18.10.m: [The hymn beginning] 'We indeed, having pressed soma, [call] upon you' consists of fifteen.
Those are twenty genuine Bṛhatī verses.

18.10.s: ye ṣaṇṇām trayaḥ pariśiṣṭās taiḥ pratipadyate |
18.10.d: ये षण्णाम् त्रयः परिशिष्टास् तैः प्रतिपद्यते ।
18.10.m: He begins with the three that were left over from the six.
[The hymn beginning] 'He who is king of the peoples' consists of three.

18.10.s: tam vo dasmam ṛtīṣaham ity ekaḥ |
18.10.d: तम् वो दस्मम् ऋतीषहम् इत्य् एकः ।
18.10.m: [The hymn beginning] 'Him to you, the wonder-worker, who withstands assaults' consists of one.

18.10.s: ā no viśvāsu havya iti trayaḥ |
18.10.d: आ नो विश्वासु हव्य इति त्रयः ।
18.10.m: [The hymn beginning] 'To us in all [battles] to be invoked' consists of three.

18.10.s: tvām id ā hyo nara iti catvāraḥ |
18.10.d: त्वाम् इद् आ ह्यो नर इति चत्वारः ।
18.10.m: [The hymn beginning] 'The men [invoked] you indeed yesterday' consists of four.
Then the six hymns of the Vālakhilyas.

18.10.s: teṣām dvau pragāthā utsṛjati indra nihavam ca vaiśvadevam ca ā no viśve sajoṣasa iti |
18.10.d: तेषाम् द्वौ प्रगाथा उत्सृजति इन्द्र निहवम् च वैश्वदेवम् च आ नो विश्वे सजोषस इति ।
18.10.m: He leaves out two Pragāthas of them: the one invoking Indra and the one to All the Gods beginning 'To us, all [gods] together with one accord'.

18.11.m: Then he recites genuine Bṛhatī verses:

18.11.s: matsy apāyi te maho asmā asmā id andhaso balam dhehi tanūṣu no yujāno haritā rathe tava id indra aham āśasā amāsu pakvam airaya iyam yā nīcy arkiṇī pra te ratham mithū kṛtam antar yaccha jighāṃsatas tvam viśvasya jagata iti daśa eka pātinyaḥ |
18.11.d: मत्स्य् अपायि ते महो अस्मा अस्मा इद् अन्धसो बलम् धेहि तनूषु नो युजानो हरिता रथे तव इद् इन्द्र अहम् आशसा अमासु पक्वम् ऐरय इयम् या नीच्य् अर्किणी प्र ते रथम् मिथू कृतम् अन्तर् यच्छ जिघांसतस् त्वम् विश्वस्य जगत इति दश एक पातिन्यः ।
18.11.m: The ten single verses [beginning]: 'Exhilarate, it has been drunk', 'Great [wealth] for this one', 'To this presser of soma', 'Put strength in our bodies', 'Yoking the two bay horses to your chariot', 'Yours indeed, O Indra, am I by prayer', 'In the raw [cows] you placed the cooked [milk]', 'This low-hanging, praising [dawn]', 'Forth your chariot', 'Turn away the double-dealing, intending to strike', and 'You of the whole world'.

18.11.s: ayam te astu haryata ā mandrair indra haribhir iti sūkte |
18.11.d: अयम् ते अस्तु हर्यत आ मन्द्रैर् इन्द्र हरिभिर् इति सूक्ते ।
18.11.m: The two hymns [beginning] 'May this be pleasant to you' and 'With charming, bay horses, O Indra'.

18.11.s: te ardharcaśaḥ śastvā atha sūda dohasam |
18.11.d: ते अर्धर्चशः शस्त्वा अथ सूद दोहसम् ।
18.11.m: Having recited them by half-verses, then [he recites] the Sūdadohas verse.

18.12.s: indraḥ suteṣu someṣv ity etayā auṣṇihīm aśītim pratipadyate |
18.12.d: इन्द्रः सुतेषु सोमेष्व् इत्य् एतया औष्णिहीम् अशीतिम् प्रतिपद्यते ।
18.12.m: With [the verse beginning] 'Indra in the pressed somas' he begins the Auṣṇihī eighty.

18.12.s: ya indra somapātama ity ekādaśa teṣām ekam utsṛjati indram vṛtrāya hantava iti |
18.12.d: य इन्द्र सोमपातम इत्य् एकादश तेषाम् एकम् उत्सृजति इन्द्रम् वृत्राय हन्तव इति ।
18.12.m: [The hymn beginning] 'He who, O Indra, is the greatest soma-drinker' consists of eleven; he leaves out one of them, namely 'Indra, to slay Vṛtra'.

18.12.s: tam v abhi pra gāyata iti catvāri |
18.12.d: तम् व् अभि प्र गायत इति चत्वारि ।
18.12.m: [The hymn beginning] 'Sing forth to him' consists of four.
[The hymn beginning] 'O friends, we pray' consists of nine.

18.12.s: ya eka id vidayata ā yāhy adribhiḥ sutam iti dve tṛce |
18.12.d: य एक इद् विदयत आ याह्य् अद्रिभिः सुतम् इति द्वे तृचे ।
18.12.m: [The hymns beginning] 'He who alone distributes' and 'Come to the [soma] pressed with stones' are two tṛcas.

18.13.m: Then he recites one hundred and four Gāyatrī verses.

18.13.s: nakir indra tvad uttara iti ṣaṭ |
18.13.d: नकिर् इन्द्र त्वद् उत्तर इति षट् ।
18.13.m: [The hymn beginning] ‘No one is higher than you, O Indra’ (nakir indra tvad uttaraḥ) consists of six [verses];

18.13.s: divaś cid ghā duhitaram iti caturdaśa |
18.13.d: दिवश् चिद् घा दुहितरम् इति चतुर्दश ।
18.13.m: ‘Even of the daughter of the sky’ (divaś cid ghā duhitaram) consists of fourteen;

18.13.s: ā tū na indra vṛtrahann ity eka viṃśatiḥ |
18.13.d: आ तू न इन्द्र वृत्रहन्न् इत्य् एक विंशतिः ।
18.13.m: ‘Come now to us, O Indra, Vṛtra-slayer’ (ā tū na indra vṛtrahan) consists of twenty-one;

18.13.s: ā va indram krivim yathā yad indra aham yathā tvam iti pañcadaśarce |
18.13.d: आ व इन्द्रम् क्रिविम् यथा यद् इन्द्र अहम् यथा त्वम् इति पञ्चदशर्चे ।
18.13.m: ‘[We invoke] you, Indra, like Krivi’ (ā va indraṃ krivim yathā) and ‘If, O Indra, I [were like you]’ (yad indrāham yathā tvam) are two hymns of fifteen verses each;

18.13.s: pra saṃrājam carṣaṇīnām uttvā mandantu stomā iti dvādaśarce |
18.13.d: प्र संराजम् चर्षणीनाम् उत्त्वा मन्दन्तु स्तोमा इति द्वादशर्चे ।
18.13.m: ‘For the sovereign ruler of men’ (pra saṃrājam carṣaṇīnām) and ‘Let the praises gladden you’ (ud u tvā mandantu stomāḥ) are two hymns of twelve verses each;

18.13.s: ā pra drava parāvata iti nava |
18.13.d: आ प्र द्रव परावत इति नव ।
18.13.m: ‘Hasten here from afar’ (ā pra drava parāvataḥ) consists of nine;
thus are the one hundred and four Gāyatrī [verses].

18.13.s: vayam u tvām apūrvyā ity aṣṭau kākubhāḥ pragāthāḥ |
18.13.d: वयम् उ त्वाम् अपूर्व्या इत्य् अष्टौ काकुभाः प्रगाथाः ।
18.13.m: [Beginning with] ‘We indeed [praise] you, the peerless’ (vayam u tvām apūrvya), there are eight Kakubh Pragātha pairs;
‘Sing a Sāman to Indra’ (indrāya sāma gāyata) is recited entirely.

18.13.s: tad ardharcaśaḥ śastvā ataḥ sūda dohasam |
18.13.d: तद् अर्धर्चशः शस्त्वा अतः सूद दोहसम् ।
18.13.m: Having recited that by half-verses, thereafter [he recites] the Sūdadohas verse.

18.14.m: Then he recites this hymn of Vaśa by half-verses:
Its seventeenth [verse] is a Jagatī; [he recites] that quarter-verse by quarter-verse.

18.14.s: atha ekaviṃśī dvāviṃśī caturviṃśī ca paṅktayas tāḥ paṅkti śaṃsam |
18.14.d: अथ एकविंशी द्वाविंशी चतुर्विंशी च पङ्क्तयस् ताः पङ्क्ति शंसम् ।
18.14.m: Then the twenty-first, twenty-second, and twenty-fourth are Paṅktis; [he recites] them with the Paṅkti-recitation.

18.14.s: śatam dāse balbūtha iti pañca padā tasyai trīṇi padāni samasya avasyed dvābhyām praṇuyāt |
18.14.d: शतम् दासे बल्बूथ इति पञ्च पदा तस्यै त्रीणि पदानि समस्य अवस्येद् द्वाभ्याम् प्रणुयात् ।
18.14.m: ‘A hundred upon the Dāsa Balbūtha’ (śataṃ dāse balbūthe) has five quarters; joining three quarters of it together, he should pause, and conclude with the praṇava after two.

18.14.s: trayodaśī ca triṃśattamī ca dvipade te pacchaḥ śastvā atha sūda dohasam |
18.14.d: त्रयोदशी च त्रिंशत्तमी च द्विपदे ते पच्छः शस्त्वा अथ सूद दोहसम् ।
18.14.m: The thirteenth and the thirtieth are Dvipadās; having recited those two quarter-verse by quarter-verse, then [he recites] the Sūdadohas verse.

18.14.s: atha etau vihṛtāv ardharcāv atha sūda dohasam |
18.14.d: अथ एतौ विहृताव् अर्धर्चाव् अथ सूद दोहसम् ।
18.14.m: Then [reciting] these two half-verses transposed, then [he recites] the Sūdadohas verse.

18.14.s: atra catur viṃśati kṛtvaḥ śastā bhavati |
18.14.d: अत्र चतुर् विंशति कृत्वः शस्ता भवति ।
18.14.m: At this point it has been recited twenty-four times.

18.15.m: Then he recites these Dvipadā verses:

18.15.s: imā nu kam bhuvanā sīṣadhāma iti pañca |
18.15.d: इमा नु कम् भुवना सीषधाम इति पञ्च ।
18.15.m: ‘Now indeed may we guide these creatures’ (imā nu kam bhuvanā sīṣadhāma) consists of five;

18.15.s: ā yāhi vanasā saha iti catasraḥ |
18.15.d: आ याहि वनसा सह इति चतस्रः ।
18.15.m: ‘Come with desire’ (ā yāhi vanasā saha) consists of four;

18.15.s: eṣa brahmā ya ṛtviya iti tisraḥ |
18.15.d: एष ब्रह्मा य ऋत्विय इति तिस्रः ।

18.15.s: pra va indrāya vṛtrahantamāya viprā gātham gāyata yaj jujoṣati | arcanty arkam marutaḥ svarkā ā stobhati śruto yuvā sa indraḥ | upaprakṣe madhumati kṣiyantaḥ puṣyema rayim dhīmahe ta indra | viśvato dāvan viśvato na ā bhara yam tvā śaviṣṭham īmahe | sa supraṇītī nṛtamaḥ svarāḷ asi maṃhiṣṭho vāja sātaye | tvam hi rādhasyata eka īśiṣe sanād amṛkta ojasā | iti ṣaṭ |
18.15.d: प्र व इन्द्राय वृत्रहन्तमाय विप्रा गाथम् गायत यज् जुजोषति । अर्चन्त्य् अर्कम् मरुतः स्वर्का आ स्तोभति श्रुतो युवा स इन्द्रः । उपप्रक्षे मधुमति क्षियन्तः पुष्येम रयिम् धीमहे त इन्द्र । विश्वतो दावन् विश्वतो न आ भर यम् त्वा शविष्ठम् ईमहे । स सुप्रणीती नृतमः स्वराऌ असि मंहिष्ठो वाज सातये । त्वम् हि राधस्यत एक ईशिषे सनाद् अमृक्त ओजसा । इति षट् ।
18.15.m:
‘This is the priest who is fit for the season’ (eṣa brahmā ya ṛtviyaḥ) consists of three; / ‘Sing, O inspired poets, a song to Indra, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, which he will enjoy. / The Maruts of beautiful praise sing a chant; the famous youthful Indra stomps:’
‘Dwelling in sweet abundance may we increase wealth; we ponder on you, O Indra. / Giver from every side, bring to us from every side that which we ask of you, the mightiest. / With good guidance, most manly, you are the independent ruler, most generous for winning booty. / For you alone have power over the bounty, untouched since old by your might’—thus six [verses];

18.15.s: ā dhūrṣv asmai vajram eko ayā vājam deva hitam sanema iti |
18.15.d: आ धूर्ष्व् अस्मै वज्रम् एको अया वाजम् देव हितम् सनेम इति ।
18.15.m: [and] ‘The vajra onto the yokes for him, he alone went; may we win the god-given prize’ (ā dhūrṣv asmai vajram eko ayā vājam devahitam sanema).
Those are twenty-one Dvipadās; [he recites] them quarter-verse by quarter-verse.

18.16.s: atha etad aindrāgnam sūktam gāyatrī śaṃsam śaṃsati indra agnī yuvam su na iti |
18.16.d: अथ एतद् ऐन्द्राग्नम् सूक्तम् गायत्री शंसम् शंसति इन्द्र अग्नी युवम् सु न इति ।
18.16.m: Then he recites this hymn to Indra and Agni with the Gāyatrī-recitation: ‘O Indra and Agni, you two well to us’ (indrāgnī yuvaṃ su naḥ).

18.16.s: tasya dvitīyā sapta padā tasyā anuṣṭubham pūrvām karoti śaṃsam gāyatrīm uttarām |
18.16.d: तस्य द्वितीया सप्त पदा तस्या अनुष्टुभम् पूर्वाम् करोति शंसम् गायत्रीम् उत्तराम् ।
18.16.m: Its second [verse] has seven quarters; he makes the prior recitation an Anuṣṭubh and the subsequent one a Gāyatrī.
The final [verse] is a Triṣṭubh; [he recites] that quarter-verse by quarter-verse.

18.17.s: tubhya idam indra pari ṣicyate madhv ity ekā |
18.17.d: तुभ्य इदम् इन्द्र परि षिच्यते मध्व् इत्य् एका ।
18.17.m: ‘For you, O Indra, this sweet [soma] is poured out around’ (tubhyedam indra pari ṣicyate madhu) is one verse;

18.17.s: viśvajite dhana jite svar jita iti ṣaṭ |
18.17.d: विश्वजिते धन जिते स्वर् जित इति षट् ।
18.17.m: ‘To the all-conquering, prize-conquering, realm-conquering’ (viśvajite dhanajite svarjite) consists of six;

18.17.s: svādor itthā viṣūvata iti pāṅktam tṛcam tat paṅkti śaṃsam |
18.17.d: स्वादोर् इत्था विषूवत इति पाङ्क्तम् तृचम् तत् पङ्क्ति शंसम् ।
18.17.m: ‘Of the sweet, indeed, of the solstice’ (svādor itthā viṣūvataḥ) is a triplet in Paṅkti metre; [he recites] that with the Paṅkti-recitation.

18.17.s: pra vo mahe mahivṛdhe bharadhvam iti vairājam tṛcam tad ardharcaśaḥ |
18.17.d: प्र वो महे महिवृधे भरध्वम् इति वैराजम् तृचम् तद् अर्धर्चशः ।
18.17.m: ‘Offer to the great one who increases greatness’ (pra vo mahe mahivṛdhe bharadhvam) is a triplet in Vairāja metre; [he recites] that by half-verses.

18.17.s: praty asmai pipīṣata ity ānuṣṭubham tṛcam tad ardharcaśaḥ |
18.17.d: प्रत्य् अस्मै पिपीषत इत्य् आनुष्टुभम् तृचम् तद् अर्धर्चशः ।
18.17.m: ‘To him who desires to drink’ (praty asmai pipīṣate) is a triplet in Anuṣṭubh metre; [he recites] that by half-verses.

18.18.m: Then he recites this collection of Anuṣṭubhs:

18.18.s: ehi stomān abhi svara iti nava |
18.18.d: एहि स्तोमान् अभि स्वर इति नव ।
18.18.m: ‘Come, greet the praises’ (ehi stomān abhi svara) consists of nine;
‘All [chants] have magnified Indra’ (indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan) consists of eight;

18.18.s: asāvi soma indra ta iti ṣaṭ | ā nas te gantu matsara iti catasraḥ |
18.18.d: असावि सोम इन्द्र त इति षट् । आ नस् ते गन्तु मत्सर इति चतस्रः ।
18.18.m: ‘Soma has been pressed, O Indra, for you’ (asāvi soma indra te) consists of six; ‘Let your exhilarating [drop] come to us’ (ā nas te gantu matsaraḥ) consists of four;

18.18.s: matsi no vasya iṣṭaya iti pañca |
18.18.d: मत्सि नो वस्य इष्टय इति पञ्च ।
18.18.m: ‘Exhilarate us for the seeking of wealth’ (matsi no vasya iṣṭaye) consists of five;

18.18.s: yas te sādhiṣṭho avasa iti sapta |
18.18.d: यस् ते साधिष्ठो अवस इति सप्त ।
18.18.m: ‘Which is your most effective [aid] for protection’ (yas te sādhiṣṭho avase) consists of seven;

18.18.s: uroṣ ṭa indra rādhasa iti dve |
18.18.d: उरोष् ट इन्द्र राधस इति द्वे ।
18.18.m: ‘Broad is your bounty, O Indra’ (uroṣ ṭa indra rādhasaḥ) consists of two;

18.18.s: yad indra citra mehana iti cataraḥ |
18.18.d: यद् इन्द्र चित्र मेहन इति चतरः ।
18.18.m: ‘O Indra of wonderful gifts’ (yad indra citra mehanā) consists of four;
‘He who is wealthy, most wealthy’ (yo rayivo rayiṃtamaḥ) consists of six;

18.18.s: ā indra yāhi haribhir iti pañcadaśa |
18.18.d: आ इन्द्र याहि हरिभिर् इति पञ्चदश ।
18.18.m: ‘Come, O Indra, with your bay steeds’ (endra yāhi haribhiḥ) consists of fifteen;
‘As of old, the increaser of poets’ (sa pratnathā kavivṛdhaḥ) is a triplet;
‘When you were born peerless’ (yaj jāyathā apūrvya) consists of two;

18.18.s: ā tvā giro rathīr iva iti sarvam |
18.18.d: आ त्वा गिरो रथीर् इव इति सर्वम् ।
18.18.m: ‘To you the songs, like a charioteer’ (ā tvā giro rathīr iva) is recited entirely;

18.18.s: śāsa itthā mahān asi iti sarvam |
18.18.d: शास इत्था महान् असि इति सर्वम् ।
18.18.m: ‘Direct thus, you are great’ (śāsā itthā mahān asi) is recited entirely;

18.19.m: Then he recites this century of Triṣṭubh verses:

18.19.s: adhvaryavo bharata indrāya somam iti ca |
18.19.d: अध्वर्यवो भरत इन्द्राय सोमम् इति च ।
18.19.m: and [the hymn] ‘Bring soma, O Adhvaryus, to Indra’ (adhvaryavo bharatendrāya somam);

18.19.s: ā yāhy arvān upa vandhureṣṭhā yudhmasya te vṛṣabhasya svarāja iti sūkte |
18.19.d: आ याह्य् अर्वान् उप वन्धुरेष्ठा युध्मस्य ते वृषभस्य स्वराज इति सूक्ते ।
18.19.m: the two hymns: ‘Come hitherward, standing on the chariot seat’ (ā yāhy arvāṅ upa vandhureṣṭhāḥ) and ‘Of your bull-like, belligerent sovereign’ (yudhmasya te vṛṣabhasya svarājaḥ);

18.19.s: nṛṇām u tvā nṛtamam gīrbhir ukthair iti tṛcam |
18.19.d: नृणाम् उ त्वा नृतमम् गीर्भिर् उक्थैर् इति तृचम् ।
18.19.m: the triplet: ‘You, the most manly of men, with songs and chants’ (nṝṇām u tvā nṛtamaṃ gīrbhir ukthaiḥ);

18.19.s: ā satyo yātu maghavān ṛjīṣī iti sarvam |
18.19.d: आ सत्यो यातु मघवान् ऋजीषी इति सर्वम् ।
18.19.m: ‘Let the truthful Maghavan who drinks the dregs come’ (ā satyo yātu maghavān ṛjīṣī) is recited entirely;

18.19.s: yoniṣ ṭa indra sadane akāry ud u brahmāṇi iti sūkte |
18.19.d: योनिष् ट इन्द्र सदने अकार्य् उद् उ ब्रह्माणि इति सूक्ते ।
18.19.m: [and] the two hymns: ‘A seat has been prepared for you, O Indra, in the dwelling’ (yoniṣ ṭa indra sadane akāri) and ‘Up the sacred utterances’ (ud u brahmāṇi).

18.19.s: tatra purastād ud brahmīyasya pada anuṣaṅgān śaṃsati yo vyatīṃr aphāṇayad ity etasmiṃs tṛce prathamāyā ardharcam uktvā uparamati |
18.19.d: तत्र पुरस्ताद् उद् ब्रह्मीयस्य पद अनुषङ्गान् शंसति यो व्यतींर् अफाणयद् इत्य् एतस्मिंस् तृचे प्रथमाया अर्धर्चम् उक्त्वा उपरमति ।
18.19.m: There, before the Ud-brahmīya, he recites the verse-quarter intertwinings: in the tṛca 'yo vyatīṁr aphāṇayat', having recited the half-verse of the first [verse], he pauses.

18.20.s: atha prathamāyai tṛtīyena padena dvitīyāyai prathamam padam upasaṃdhāya praṇauti |
18.20.d: अथ प्रथमायै तृतीयेन पदेन द्वितीयायै प्रथमम् पदम् उपसंधाय प्रणौति ।
18.20.m: Then, having joined the first quarter of the second [verse] to the third quarter of the first, he recites the praṇava.

18.20.s: atha prathamāyā uttamena padena dvitīyāyai dvitīyam padam upasaṃdhāya avasyati |
18.20.d: अथ प्रथमाया उत्तमेन पदेन द्वितीयायै द्वितीयम् पदम् उपसंधाय अवस्यति ।
18.20.m: Then, having joined the second quarter of the second [verse] to the last quarter of the first, he stops.

18.20.s: atha dvitīyāyai tṛtīyena padena uttamāyai pathamam padam upasaṃdhāya praṇauti |
18.20.d: अथ द्वितीयायै तृतीयेन पदेन उत्तमायै पथमम् पदम् उपसंधाय प्रणौति ।
18.20.m: Then, having joined the first quarter of the last [verse] to the third quarter of the second, he recites the praṇava.

18.20.s: atha dvitīyāyā uttamena padena uttamāyai dvitīyam padam upasaṃdhāya avasyati |
18.20.d: अथ द्वितीयाया उत्तमेन पदेन उत्तमायै द्वितीयम् पदम् उपसंधाय अवस्यति ।
18.20.m: Then, having joined the second quarter of the last [verse] to the last quarter of the second, he stops.
Then what remains is [recited] by half-verses; with that he recites the praṇava.

18.20.s: atho ud brahmīyasya uttamām pariśiṣya āhvayate |
18.20.d: अथो उद् ब्रह्मीयस्य उत्तमाम् परिशिष्य आह्वयते ।
18.20.m: Then, leaving aside the final [verse] of the Ud-brahmīya, he utters the call.
He concludes with [that verse] recited three times.

18.20.s: paridhāya uktha vīryam japaty aikāhikam pūrvam māhāvratikam uttaram mahad asi yaśo asi bhargo asi bhogo asi bhuñjad asi mama bhogāya bhava iti |
18.20.d: परिधाय उक्थ वीर्यम् जपत्य् ऐकाहिकम् पूर्वम् माहाव्रतिकम् उत्तरम् महद् असि यशो असि भर्गो असि भोगो असि भुञ्जद् असि मम भोगाय भव इति ।
18.20.m: Having concluded, he mutters the power of the uktha: first the one for the single-day rite, then the Mahāvrata one: 'Great art thou, glory art thou, radiance art thou, enjoyment art thou, enjoying art thou; be thou for my enjoyment'.

18.21.s: tad etat sakṛt śastāyām sūda dohasi yāvat śastram upasarjanyām saṃkhyāyamānāyām ṛte tūṣṇīm śaṃsam bṛhatī sahasram sampadyate |
18.21.d: तद् एतत् सकृत् शस्तायाम् सूद दोहसि यावत् शस्त्रम् उपसर्जन्याम् संख्यायमानायाम् ऋते तूष्णीम् शंसम् बृहती सहस्रम् सम्पद्यते ।
18.21.m: This recitation, when the Sūdadohas is recited once and the appended verse is counted, without the silent recitation, amounts to one thousand bṛhatī verses.
for the stotriya, for the nivid, [and] for the concluding verse.
Even while the secondary vaṣaṭ-call has not been made, they untie the swing.
As [the Adhvaryu] approaches holding the cup, he steps down towards the east.
He pushes the swing-board away to the west.

18.21.s: parāmṛśan graham japati yad imam prajayam prājaiṣam tam anvasāni iti |
18.21.d: परामृशन् ग्रहम् जपति यद् इमम् प्रजयम् प्राजैषम् तम् अन्वसानि इति ।
18.21.m: Touching the cup, he mutters: 'That offspring which I have won, may I pursue that'.

18.21.s: adhvarya upahavam iṣṭvā bhakṣayaty ojase tvā iti |
18.21.d: अध्वर्य उपहवम् इष्ट्वा भक्षयत्य् ओजसे त्वा इति ।
18.21.m: Having requested the invitation from the Adhvaryu, he consumes [it with the mantra]: 'For vigor thee'.
The extra draught belongs to Viśvakarman.

18.21.s: tasya bhakṣa upa mā yantu majjayaḥ sanīlā upa mā jakṣur upa mā manīṣā priyām aham tanvam paśyamāno mayi ramo devānām ojase tvā iti |
18.21.d: तस्य भक्ष उप मा यन्तु मज्जयः सनीला उप मा जक्षुर् उप मा मनीषा प्रियाम् अहम् तन्वम् पश्यमानो मयि रमो देवानाम् ओजसे त्वा इति ।
18.21.m: The consumption formula for it is: 'May the nest-sharing marrows come to me; may consumption come to me, may insight come to me; beholding my beloved body, may delight of the gods be in me; for vigor thee'.

18.21.s: atha camasān bhakṣayanti devo asi narā śaṃsa iti |
18.21.d: अथ चमसान् भक्षयन्ति देवो असि नरा शंस इति ।
18.21.m: Then they consume the goblets [with]: 'A god art thou, Narāśaṁsa'.

18.22.s: tat savitur vṛṇīmahe adyā no deva savitar iti tṛcau pratipad anucarau vaiśvadevasya |
18.22.d: तत् सवितुर् वृणीमहे अद्या नो देव सवितर् इति तृचौ प्रतिपद् अनुचरौ वैश्वदेवस्य ।
18.22.m: 'tat savitur vṛṇīmahe' and 'adyā no deva savitar' are the two tṛcas for the opening verse and the following verse of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra.
This is indeed the regular extension for a single-day rite.

18.22.s: tad devasya savitur vāryam mahad iti sāvitram |
18.22.d: तद् देवस्य सवितुर् वार्यम् महद् इति सावित्रम् ।
18.22.m: 'tad devasya savitur vāryam mahat' is the hymn to Savitṛ.

18.22.s: te hi dyāvā pṛthivī viśva śambhuvā iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam |
18.22.d: ते हि द्यावा पृथिवी विश्व शम्भुवा इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् ।
18.22.m: 'te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuvā' is the hymn to Heaven and Earth.

18.22.s: kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kim yaviṣṭho na ājagann ity ārbhavam |
18.22.d: किम् उ श्रेष्ठः किम् यविष्ठो न आजगन्न् इत्य् आर्भवम् ।
18.22.m: 'kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kim yaviṣṭho na ājagan' is the hymn to the Ṛbhus.

18.22.s: asya vāmasya palitasya hotur iti salilam vaiśvadevam tasyāḥ samudrā adhi vi kṣaranti samānam etad udakam ity ete ardharcaśaḥ aṃsati paccha itarāḥ |
18.22.d: अस्य वामस्य पलितस्य होतुर् इति सलिलम् वैश्वदेवम् तस्याः समुद्रा अधि वि क्षरन्ति समानम् एतद् उदकम् इत्य् एते अर्धर्चशः अंसति पच्छ इतराः ।
18.22.m: 'asya vāmasya palitasya hotuḥ' is the Salila-vaiśvadeva hymn; [the verses] 'tasyāḥ samudrā adhi vi kṣaranti' and 'samānam etad udakam' he recites by half-verses, the others quarter by quarter.

18.22.s: tat śastvā ā no bhadrīye nividam dadhāti |
18.22.d: तत् शस्त्वा आ नो भद्रीये निविदम् दधाति ।
18.22.m: Having recited that, he inserts the nivid into [the hymn] 'ā no bhadrāḥ'.
The hymn to the five peoples is the concluding verse.

18.23.s: vaiśvānarāya pṛthu pājase vipa iti vaiśvānarīyam |
18.23.d: वैश्वानराय पृथु पाजसे विप इति वैश्वानरीयम् ।
18.23.m: 'vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase vipaḥ' is the hymn to Vaiśvānara.

18.23.s: prayajyavo maruto bhrāja dṛṣṭaya iti mārutam |
18.23.d: प्रयज्यवो मरुतो भ्राज दृष्टय इति मारुतम् ।
18.23.m: 'prayajyavo maruto bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ' is the hymn to the Maruts.

18.23.s: te yadi yajñāyajñīyam agniṣṭoma sāma kuryus tasya uktau stotriya anurūpau |
18.23.d: ते यदि यज्ञायज्ञीयम् अग्निष्टोम साम कुर्युस् तस्य उक्तौ स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ ।
18.23.m: If they should perform the Yajñāyajñīya as the Agniṣṭoma-sāman, its stotriya and corresponding verses have already been stated.

18.23.s: yady u vā iḷāṃdam agne tava śravo vaya iti stotriyas tṛco ata eva uttaraḥ sūkta anurūpaḥ |
18.23.d: यद्य् उ वा इऌआंदम् अग्ने तव श्रवो वय इति स्तोत्रियस् तृचो अत एव उत्तरः सूक्त अनुरूपः ।
18.23.m: Or if [the sāman is] Iḷānda, 'agne tava śravo vayaḥ' is the stotriya tṛca; immediately following is the corresponding verse-group of the hymn.

18.23.s: yady u sarvasmin ṣaḷarce stuvīran na agnim na svavṛktibhir ity etasya ṣaḷ anurūpam kurvīta |
18.23.d: यद्य् उ सर्वस्मिन् षऌअर्चे स्तुवीरन् न अग्निम् न स्ववृक्तिभिर् इत्य् एतस्य षऌ अनुरूपम् कुर्वीत ।
18.23.m: And if they chant on the whole six-verse hymn, he should make the corresponding group of six [from] 'na agniṁ na svavṛktibhiḥ'.

18.23.s: yady u vā aticchandahsu kuryur agnim hotāram manye dāsvantam iti stotriyas tṛco ata eva uttaraḥ sūkta anurūpaḥ |
18.23.d: यद्य् उ वा अतिच्छन्दह्सु कुर्युर् अग्निम् होतारम् मन्ये दास्वन्तम् इति स्तोत्रियस् तृचो अत एव उत्तरः सूक्त अनुरूपः ।
18.23.m: Or if they perform it in hypermetric metres: 'agniṁ hotāraṁ manye dāsvantam' is the stotriya tṛca; immediately following is the corresponding verse-group of the hymn.

18.23.s: yā saptamī sūktasya tām tṛtīyām karoti so anurūpaḥ |
18.23.d: या सप्तमी सूक्तस्य ताम् तृतीयाम् करोति सो अनुरूपः ।
18.23.m: The seventh [verse] of the hymn he makes the third; that is the corresponding verse-group.

18.23.s: ayam jāyata manuṣo dharīmaṇi iti vā stotriyas tṛco ata eva uttaraḥ sūkta anurūpaḥ |
18.23.d: अयम् जायत मनुषो धरीमणि इति वा स्तोत्रियस् तृचो अत एव उत्तरः सूक्त अनुरूपः ।
18.23.m: Or 'ayaṁ jāyata manuṣo dharīmaṇi' is the stotriya tṛca; immediately following is the corresponding verse-group of the hymn.
Here he should not recite the origin-verse of the Yajñāyajñīya.

18.23.s: baḷ itthā tad vapuṣe dhāyi darśatam iti jāta vedasīyam |
18.23.d: बऌ इत्था तद् वपुषे धायि दर्शतम् इति जात वेदसीयम् ।
18.23.m: 'baḷ itthā tad vapuṣe dhāyi darśatam' is the hymn to Jātavedas.
These are the hymns of the Āgnimāruta-śastra.
These are the hymns of this day.

18.24.m: Then in the morning they undertake the concluding Atirātra.

18.24.s: ya eva asau prāyaṇīyaḥ sa udayanīyaḥ |
18.24.d: य एव असौ प्रायणीयः स उदयनीयः ।
18.24.m: Whatever was the introductory rite, that same is the concluding rite.

18.24.s: tatra sarvān karasnān sambādhya preṣyati maitrāvaruṇaḥ |
18.24.d: तत्र सर्वान् करस्नान् सम्बाध्य प्रेष्यति मैत्रावरुणः ।
18.24.m: There, having touched all the hands, the Maitrāvaruṇa gives the ritual summons.

18.24.s: te prathama māsam dīkṣita vasanāni vā vasate |
18.24.d: ते प्रथम मासम् दीक्षित वसनानि वा वसते ।
18.24.m: For the first month they wear the garments of the consecrated.
They lay them aside for the nine-day period.

18.24.s: atha itarān māsān ajināni vā ārdra vasanāni vā vasate |
18.24.d: अथ इतरान् मासान् अजिनानि वा आर्द्र वसनानि वा वसते ।
18.24.m: Then during the other months they wear skins or fresh garments.
For in that [period] the concluding rites are performed.
They do not draw the vasatīvarī waters for the following day.
They offer the concluding oblations.
The ritual of the purificatory bath is performed.

18.24.s: te yadi yajña agārair bhokṣyamāṇā bhavanty ādadhata eva preṅkha miśram |
18.24.d: ते यदि यज्ञ अगारैर् भोक्ष्यमाणा भवन्त्य् आदधत एव प्रेङ्ख मिश्रम् ।
18.24.m: If they intend to enjoy [the use of] the sacrificial halls, they just put aside [the implements] mixed with the swing.

18.24.s: yady u dhakṣyanto atra eva syāt |
18.24.d: यद्य् उ धक्ष्यन्तो अत्र एव स्यात् ।
18.24.m: If, however, they intend to burn [them], it should remain right there.

18.24.s: tasyai vapāyām saṃsthitāyām dakṣiṇa ardha apara ardhād vedeḥ kiṃcit pariśritya tasminn upaviśya keśa śmaśrūṇi vāpayanti |
18.24.d: तस्यै वपायाम् संस्थितायाम् दक्षिण अर्ध अपर अर्धाद् वेदेः किंचित् परिश्रित्य तस्मिन्न् उपविश्य केश श्मश्रूणि वापयन्ति ।
18.24.m: When its omentum has been completed, having enclosed a space somewhat to the southwest of the sacrificial altar and having sat down in it, they have their hair and beards shaved,
and all body hair, and they pare their nails.
They wrap turbans [around their heads] until the hair grows back.
They complete the remainder of the subsequently bound victim.
It ends with the heart-spit.

18.24.s: tasyām saṃsthitāyām yathā samprakīrṇam agnīn samāropya antareṇa cātvālautkarā upaniṣkrāmanti |
18.24.d: तस्याम् संस्थितायाम् यथा सम्प्रकीर्णम् अग्नीन् समारोप्य अन्तरेण चात्वालौत्करा उपनिष्क्रामन्ति ।
18.24.m: When it is completed, having taken up the fires as they are scattered, they go out between the pit and the rubbish heap.

18.24.s: uttarata udghāta avokṣite agny āyatanāni kṛtvā gomayena upalipya mathitvā agnīn vihṛtya praṇītāḥ praṇīya pūrṇa āhutīr hutvā pṛthag udavasānīyābhir yajante ya āhita agnayo bhavanti |
18.24.d: उत्तरत उद्घात अवोक्षिते अग्न्य् आयतनानि कृत्वा गोमयेन उपलिप्य मथित्वा अग्नीन् विहृत्य प्रणीताः प्रणीय पूर्ण आहुतीर् हुत्वा पृथग् उदवसानीयाभिर् यजन्ते य आहित अग्नयो भवन्ति ।
18.24.m: To the north, having leveled and sprinkled [a spot], made the fire-places, smeared [them] with cow dung, churned [the fire], distributed the fires, brought forward the Praṇītā water, and offered the full oblations, those who have set up the sacred fires sacrifice separately with the concluding departure sacrifices.

18.24.s: atha ye anāhita agnayo gṛhapatim eva ta upāsate |
18.24.d: अथ ये अनाहित अग्नयो गृहपतिम् एव त उपासते ।
18.24.m: Now those who have not set up the sacred fires attend upon the householder [of the sacrificial session] alone.

18.24.s: sa kāmam eva pṛṣṭha śamanīyena yajeta |
18.24.d: स कामम् एव पृष्ठ शमनीयेन यजेत ।
18.24.m: At his pleasure, he may sacrifice with the Pṛṣṭhaśamanīya [offering];

18.24.s: yadi tu yajeta eta eva asya satriṇa ṛtvijaḥ syuḥ |
18.24.d: यदि तु यजेत एत एव अस्य सत्रिण ऋत्विजः स्युः ।
18.24.m: If, however, he sacrifices, these very sacrificers of the session shall be his priests.

18.24.s: tebhyas tad dadyād yad deyam syāt |
18.24.d: तेभ्यस् तद् दद्याद् यद् देयम् स्यात् ।
18.24.m: He should give them whatever is to be given.
Here the one-year [session] is concluded.

18.24.s: atha ato hotrāṇām eva mīmāṃsā | tasya atas tasya ataḥ |
18.24.d: अथ अतो होत्राणाम् एव मीमांसा । तस्य अतस् तस्य अतः ।
18.24.m: Now, therefore, is the investigation of the Hotṛ offices alone. Of it, from it; of it, from it.
